status_summary: No enacted law, bill or federal contracting rule imposing a citizenship share on contractor workforces was found. H.R. 9063, the Hire American Act, introduced 2026-05-29, would amend Title 5 to require that federal employees be U.S. citizens or nationals, with limited exceptions; per its GovInfo listing and trade press, it covers federal employment, not contractor workforces, and it is not counted as this recommendation. No bill amending the law to let private employers prefer citizens in hiring was found. Two H-1B wage bills, S. 5638 (introduced 2026-09-30) and H.R. 10799 (introduced 2026-10-13), were referred to the Senate and House Judiciary Committees; by their bill status titles they concern the wage required for exempt H-1B workers and set no citizen share or employer preference.
title: Require 70 percent U.S. citizens among workers on new federal contracts
uncertainties: No enacted law, bill or federal contracting rule imposing a citizenship share on contractor workforces was found, and no bill letting private employers prefer citizens in hiring. The Labor and FAR Council Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) carry no such entry; the FAR overhaul cases list part numbers only and were not opened. Bill searches before 2026-10-22 were read by title, congress.gov could not be fetched, and the GSA and DOL newsrooms were not checked, so a bill the searches missed cannot be excluded. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19. Update 2026-10-22: GovInfo bill status for H.R. 9063 (Hire American Act) was opened: introduced 2026-05-29, referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, one cosponsor added 2026-06-02, no later action; its title restricts federal government employment to citizens and nationals, and the status record shows no contractor provision, though bill text was not read. Two related H-1B wage bills were also opened and differ from this recommendation: S. 5638 (introduced 2026-09-30, referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee) and H.R. 10799 (introduced 2026-10-13, referred to the House Judiciary Committee) concern the wage level for exempt H-1B workers and, by title, set no citizen share or employer preference; neither record carries a summary or text. An external retrieval ran 16 searches on 2026-10-22 (Congress.gov, Federal Register, acquisition.gov and the open web) and reported no bill or FAR case requiring a citizen share of a contractor workforce; those searches cannot be reproduced. The same retrieval reported that existing law at 8 U.S.C. 1324b already treats preferring an equally qualified citizen or national over a noncitizen as not an unfair immigration-related employment practice, which would bear on how the second remaining item is framed; the law.cornell.edu copy of that section could not be opened in this review on 2026-10-22, so that reading is unverified and the item is left as written. The retrieval also reported that FAR overhaul cases 2026-003, 2026-006, 2026-010 and 2026-011 show no citizenship workforce requirement; that point was not verified. A bill missed by title-based searches still cannot be excluded.
